++++
+title = "Multi-axis operations"
+description = "One section per multi-axis kind: what it is for, its key settings and defaults, what it picks, the reach and collision checks, and the refusals you are most likely to meet."
+weight = 5
++++
+
+This page is the reference for the kinds in the **Multi-axis** group of
+the [operations](@/guide/operations.md) ribbon: 5-Axis Contour, 5-Axis
+Parallel, 5-Axis Flow, Multi-Axis Contour, Swarf, Advanced Swarf, Rotary
+Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset and Multi-Axis Rough. For the
+tabs themselves and what a click picks, see that page; for what a refusal
+means in general, see [Reading a refusal](@/guide/refusals.md).
+
+Lengths are in mm (inches in an inch document), feeds in mm/min (in/min),
+angles in degrees. The defaults below are what a freshly created operation
+starts with: feed 1200, plunge feed 300, climb milling on, clearance 25
+above the stock top, top at the model top, bottom at the model bottom,
+stepdown 5, stepover 3 and tolerance 0.05. A retyped operation keeps the
+numbers it already had; a retype from an indexed (3+2) operation drops
+its tilt.
+
+## What every multi-axis kind shares
+
+**The tool.** Every kind cuts with a ball-nose. A wrong tool is refused
+by name ("'<tool>' is a <kind>; a <operation> operation cuts with a ...").
+
+**The pose: lead, lag and max tilt.** Each kind carries the same three
+angles on its Passes tab, all 0 / 0 / 90 on a new operation:
+
+| Setting | What it does |
+|---|---|
+| Tool lead angle | leans the tool with the feed, off the surface normal (off the radial for the rotary kinds) |
+| Tool lag angle | leans it across the feed (side tilt) |
+| Max tilt | the cone the spindle may open from the normal; where the surface asks for more, the lean folds onto the cone's edge |
+
+The ball's centre does not move when the tool leans: the pose decides
+which way the spindle points, not where the cut lands, so every kind's
+cut is verified against the model as a swept ball, within the kind's
+tolerance.
+
+**Avoid shank collisions** (5-Axis Contour, 5-Axis Parallel, 5-Axis Flow,
+Multi-Axis Contour and Multi-Axis Rough; off by default). Where the posed
+tool's shank would touch the part, the spindle tilts to the nearest clear
+angle inside the max-tilt cone; positions never move. Where no angle in
+the cone clears, generation stops: "the shank of the tool touches the part
+at move ... of the posed path, and no pose inside the max-tilt cone (...
+deg) clears it - widen the cone, shorten the tool, or turn shank avoidance
+off". With the switch off, a shank that touches is still caught by the
+verification at the post gate.
+
+**Pose swings happen in air.** A pose change of more than 30 degrees
+between moves below the clearance plane is refused ("... pose swing ...
+deg at move ... - refused: a pose turn past 30 deg happens in air, never
+on a cut"); the links retract, swing and plunge instead.
+
+**The machine must reach the pose.** A leaning move needs a machine with
+tilting rotaries. The machine check refuses each move the mounted machine
+cannot hold, by name: "move ... tilts the tool; <machine> states no
+tilting rotary", "move ... commands B ... deg; <machine> states no B
+axis", "move ... commands A ... deg, the travel is ...". A machine whose
+only rotary turns about X (a 4th-axis table) is judged through that one
+axis: "<machine>'s only rotary, A about X, cannot reach that pose". The
+built-in **Tilt-head 5-axis** machine can hold the poses; the plain VMC
+cannot, so post multi-axis work with a machine that states its rotaries.
+
+## 5-Axis Contour
+
+**For:** finishing steep walls with waterline rings, with the tool leaning
+off the wall. Choose it over 3D Finish's waterline when the holder or
+shank would rub a deep wall at a vertical pose.
+
+**Picks:** none; it rings the whole model.
+
+| Tab | Setting | Default |
+|---|---|---|
+| Heights | Clearance Z / Top Z / Bottom Z | Top is the first ring's plane, Bottom the last level's |
+| Heights | Hop below clearance (Retract Z) | off |
+| Passes | Lead / lag / max tilt | 0 / 0 / 90 |
+| Passes | Avoid shank collisions | off |
+| Passes | Tolerance | 0.05: levels drop by 2 x sqrt(tool radius x tolerance) |
+| Feeds | Feed / Plunge feed / Climb milling | 1200 / 300 / on |
+
+## 5-Axis Parallel
+
+**For:** raster finishing of open, shallow-to-moderate ground with a
+leaning tool. Choose it over 3D Finish's parallel when a lead angle keeps
+the ball off its dead centre on flat-ish ground.
+
+**Picks:** none; it covers the whole model.
+
+| Tab | Setting | Default |
+|---|---|---|
+| Passes | Stepover | Auto: from tolerance and tool by the scallop law, times the slope's cosine |
+| Passes | Lead / lag / max tilt | 0 / 0 / 90 |
+| Passes | Avoid shank collisions | off |
+| Passes | Tolerance | 0.05 |
+| Feeds | Feed / Plunge feed / Climb milling | 1200 / 300 / on |
+
+A stated stepover is the flat-ground spacing; on a slope it follows the
+terrain's cosine.
+
+## 5-Axis Flow
+
+**For:** the 5-Axis Parallel's lines, but following the surface's own
+least-curving direction instead of a straight raster. Choose it on
+blended, sweeping ground where straight lines cross the flow; flat ground
+is cut in straight passes. The settings and defaults are 5-Axis
+Parallel's; the direction is read from the model, not set.
+
+## Multi-Axis Contour
+
+**For:** riding the ball along picked model edges wherever they stand,
+with a leaning tool: a chamfer or trace along a 3D edge. Choose it over
+the 2D Trace when the edge is not in one plane.
+
+**Picks:** one or more edge chains on the Geometry tab. A new one cuts
+nothing until chains are picked: "multi-axis contour needs at least one
+picked edge chain of two distinct points".
+
+| Tab | Setting | Default |
+|---|---|---|
+| Heights | Clearance Z / Top Z / Bottom Z | the machining window; a chain outside it is refused, never clipped |
+| Passes | Lead / lag / max tilt | 0 / 0 / 90 |
+| Passes | Avoid shank collisions | off |
+| Passes | Tolerance | 0.05 (the verify budget only; it authors nothing) |
+| Feeds | Feed / Plunge feed / Climb milling | 1200 / 300 / on |
+
+**Common refusals:** "Multi-Axis Contour needs a ball-nose tool, '...' is
+a ..."; "picked chain ... stands at z ..., outside the window [..., ...]
+- widen Top/Bottom of Part Z or re-pick"; "multi-axis contour found no
+model to ride".
+
+## Swarf
+
+**For:** finishing ruled flanks (surfaces straight in one direction, such
+as a drafted wall) with passes along the ruling. Choose it on ruled
+walls; doubly-curved ground is 5-Axis Parallel work.
+
+**Picks:** none; the ruling is read off the model.
+
+| Tab | Setting | Default |
+|---|---|---|
+| Heights | Clearance Z / Top Z / Bottom Z | Top is the first line's plane, Bottom the last one's |
+| Passes | Stepover | Auto: by the scallop law, across the ruling |
+| Passes | Lead / lag / max tilt | 0 / 0 / 90 |
+| Passes | Tolerance | 0.05 |
+| Feeds | Feed / Plunge feed / Climb milling | 1200 / 300 / on |
+
+**Common refusals:** "swarf found no ruling to follow - this surface
+curves about the same in every direction; doubly-curved ground is 5-Axis
+Parallel or Scallop work"; "this model's ruling runs along Z (vertical
+walls): its flanks belong to the waterline rings, which is 5-Axis Contour
+work"; "the ruling turns across the region - no single straight pass
+direction follows it; split the ruled faces or finish with 5-Axis
+Parallel"; "the mesh is too coarse for the ruling to be seen anywhere:
+refine it or finish with 5-Axis Parallel".
+
+## Advanced Swarf
+
+**For:** Swarf run coarse to fine. Each rough pass relaxes the tolerance
+fourfold and doubles the spacing; the last pass cuts to the stated
+tolerance. Choose it over Swarf when one pass would take too much at
+once.
+
+Settings as Swarf, plus **Pass count** on the Passes tab: 2 on a new
+operation, 1 to 4 (the panel clamps it). Refusals as Swarf.
+
+## Rotary Contour
+
+**For:** finishing a turned workpiece in rings around its axis, the tool
+posed off the radial. The axis is fitted to the model, not set. Choose it
+for a part standing on its axis; a bar lying flat is Rotary Parallel work.
+
+**Picks:** none.
+
+| Tab | Setting | Default |
+|---|---|---|
+| Heights | Clearance Z / Top Z / Bottom Z | mapped onto stations along the fitted axis: Top where the run starts, Bottom where it ends |
+| Passes | Lead / lag / max tilt | 0 / 0 / 90, off the radial |
+| Passes | Tolerance | 0.05: stations drop by the scallop law |
+| Feeds | Feed / Plunge feed / Climb milling | 1200 / 300 / on |
+
+**Common refusals:** "the model's normals share no rotation axis - a
+turned workpiece is rotary work; finish a freeform with the 5-Axis
+kinds"; "every axis fits this model equally - it curves the same the
+world around; domed ground is 5-Axis Contour or Parallel work"; "the
+work's axis lies flat on the table - a laid bar is finished with passes
+along it: Rotary Parallel".
+
+## Rotary Parallel
+
+**For:** finishing a turned bar with passes along its fitted axis, spaced
+around the turn. Choose it for a bar lying on the table.
+
+Settings as Rotary Contour, plus **Stepover** (Auto: by the scallop law,
+around the turn; a stated value is the spacing around the turn). Its
+heights are read as radii about the bar's axis.
+
+**Common refusals:** "the work stands on its axis - passes along a
+standing bar are its rings: Rotary Contour"; "Rotary Parallel reads its
+... height as a radius about the bar's axis: ... mm does not clear the
+work's ... mm radius - raise it".
+
+## Rotary Offset
+
+**For:** roughing a turned bar by wrapping: each level peels a radial
+infeed off the skin, the passes spaced around the bar. Choose it to rough
+before Rotary Contour or Rotary Parallel.
+
+| Tab | Setting | Default |
+|---|---|---|
+| Heights | Clearance Z / Top Z / Bottom Z | stations along the fitted axis; the ladder roughs only between them |
+| Heights | Stepdown (radial) | 5 |
+| Passes | Stepover | 3, in developed arc length around the bar |
+| Passes | Stock to leave | 0 |
+| Passes | Strategy | Auto (Zigzag, Waterline, Adaptive, Offset rings) |
+| Passes | Lead / lag / max tilt | 0 / 0 / 90 |
+| Passes | Tolerance | 0.05 (the verify budget) |
+| Lead in / Lead out | Entry | Plunge, down the radial |
+
+**Common refusals:** "the rotary wrap needs a closed solid, but the mesh
+is open: ... edges bound one facet only (a hole in the skin)"; "a feature
+that is not turned (a flat, a keyway, a cross hole) crosses the rotary
+wrap's seam ..."; "the wrapped work has no radial extent to rough"; "the
+height window leaves no station of the work to rough".
+
+## Multi-Axis Rough
+
+**For:** the 3D Pocket's level-by-level roughing, move for move, with the
+spindle posed where a wall or corner needs it and vertical where a floor
+does not ask. Choose it over 3D Pocket when the shank or holder would
+reach a deep wall at a vertical pose.
+
+**Picks:** none; it roughs around the whole model.
+
+| Tab | Setting | Default |
+|---|---|---|
+| Heights | Stepdown | 5 |
+| Passes | Stepover / Stock to leave | 3 / 0 |
+| Passes | Strategy | Auto (Zigzag, Waterline, Adaptive, Offset rings) |
+| Passes | Lead / lag / max tilt | 0 / 0 / 90 |
+| Passes | Avoid shank collisions | off |
+| Passes | Tolerance | 0.05 (the verify budget) |
+| Lead in / Lead out | Entry | Plunge |
+
+Its refusals are the 3D Pocket's, plus the pose checks above.

++++
+title = "Plasma cutting"
+description = "The Plasma Profile operation: kerf, cut direction, leads, small holes, the plasma table and post it needs, and the refusals you are most likely to meet."
+weight = 5
++++
+
+This page is the reference for **Plasma Profile**, the one kind in the
+**Plasma** group of the [operations](@/guide/operations.md) ribbon. For
+the tabs themselves and what a click picks, see that page; for what a
+refusal means in general, see [Reading a refusal](@/guide/refusals.md).
+
+Lengths are in mm (inches in an inch document), feeds in mm/min (in/min).
+
+## The machine, the tool and the post
+
+**A plasma table.** Plasma Profile needs a setup whose machine is a
+plasma table, such as the built-in **Tormach 1300PL**; a mill, lathe or
+mill-turn is refused ("a Plasma Profile operation is plasma cutting work;
+the setup's machine is a ... - mount a plasma table first"). A plasma
+table in turn takes no other kind ("... the setup's machine is a plasma
+table, which cuts only plasma operations (a Plasma Profile)").
+
+**A torch.** The tool is a plasma torch, and its diameter is the kerf
+width. Anything else is refused ("a plasma profile mounts a plasma torch,
+not a ... - its diameter is the kerf width"); a torch states no rpm ("a
+plasma torch turns no spindle - its rpm must be 0 ...").
+
+**A plasma post.** The **Tormach PathPilot Plasma** post serves plasma
+tables, and only them. The machine check judges X/Y travel and feed
+against the table, and refuses a spindle word, a tilted or turned move, or
+more tools than the table carries. Z is the torch lifter: the control sets
+pierce and cut height, so cutting depth and Z travel are not judged, and
+the 3D stock simulation does not run for a torch. The through-cut is
+judged instead by the plasma laws at the post gate (below).
+
+## Plasma Profile
+
+**For:** cutting parts out of flat plate: one through-cut per contour,
+with the kerf offset to the waste side, arc leads, holes before the
+outline that frees the part, and a slower centre-pierced cut for small
+holes.
+
+**Picks:** the closed contours and open runs to cut, on the Geometry tab.
+Without picks it cuts the model's through-silhouette. A closed contour is
+cut with the kerf on the scrap side; an open run is cut on its centre
+line, with no kerf side and no leads.
+
+| Tab | Setting | Default |
+|---|---|---|
+| Geometry | Kerf width | Torch: the torch's diameter |
+| Geometry | Compensation | In computer (offset path); or In control (G41/G42) |
+| Geometry | Direction | Outer CW, holes CCW; or Reversed: outer CCW, holes CW |
+| Heights | Clearance (torch off) | 25 above the stock top |
+| Heights | Top of plate / Bottom of plate | model top / model bottom |
+| Heights | Pierce height / Cut height | Controller (blank) |
+| Passes | Small hole below | 32 |
+| Passes | Small hole feed | 65 % |
+| Passes | Overburn | 0 |
+| Lead in / Lead out | Lead-in length / Lead-out length | 5 / 3 |
+| Feeds | Cut feed / Pierce delay | AutoFS (blank: the controller's material table) |
+
+**Kerf.** The path is the torch centre: every lit move stands half the
+kerf off the part on the waste side. **In control** posts the part
+outline with G41/G42 and lets the control offset it; it needs straight
+leads at least the kerf radius long.
+
+**Direction.** The default runs outer contours clockwise and holes
+counter-clockwise, so the arc's square edge falls on the part and the
+bevelled edge on the scrap. **Reversed** swaps both, and the path says so.
+
+**Leads.** Arcs on the scrap side. A lead with no room beside the part is
+shortened, and the path names it ("lead-in shortened to ... mm - the
+stated ... mm found no room beside the part").
+
+**Small holes.** A hole under **Small hole below** across, or under 1.5x
+the plate thickness, leads in from near its centre, takes no lead-out
+(the **Overburn** runs past the start instead) and is cut at **Small hole
+feed** of the cut feed.
+
+**Heights and feeds.** One through-cut at the plate top; there are no
+depth steps. Blank heights, feed and pierce delay are left to the
+controller (AutoFS); a stated one must be positive ("a stated feed must
+be positive - leave it blank for the controller's").
+
+**The plasma laws.** Generation refuses any lit move whose kerf would
+reach the part, and any edge the kerf can never reach. At the post gate,
+cut order and cut crossing refuse; a kerf crossing and a tip-up warn,
+named on the line:
+
+- "contour C...: move ... would carry the kerf into the part near X... Y...
+  - refused";
+- "contour C...: the torch never comes within a kerf of the part edge near
+  X... Y... - a slot, notch or keyway narrower than the kerf (... mm) is
+  bridged by the offset, not cut; widen it past the kerf or use a narrower
+  kerf";
+- "cut order: contour C... is cut after contour C..., which encloses it -
+  a hole after its outline (or an island after its hole) cuts into a part
+  already freed";
+- "cut crossing: contour C...'s cut crosses contour C...'s - the kerf runs
+  through a part already cut";
+- "kerf crossing: contour C... comes within a kerf of contour C...'s cut -
+  the torch height control can dive into the open kerf".
+
+**Common refusals:** "plasma profile: no contour to cut"; "picked contour
+... crosses itself - a cut path cannot cross its own kerf"; "picked
+contour ... has no area (a zero-length or collinear ring) - there is
+nothing to cut around"; "control compensation (G41/G42) needs a straight
+lead-in of at least the kerf radius (... mm) - the control builds the
+offset over it; the lead-in is ... mm"; "the clearance plane (...) must
+stand above the cut plane (...)"; "plasma profile: the plate's bottom
+(...) stands above its top (...)".

@@ -0,0 +1,89 @@
++++
+title = "Probing"
+description = "The Probe operation: what it finds, its settings and defaults, what it writes into the program, and the guards around the stylus."
+weight = 5
++++
+
+This page is the reference for **Probe**, in the **Drilling** group of
+the [operations](@/guide/operations.md) ribbon. For the tabs themselves
+and what a click picks, see that page; for what a refusal means in
+general, see [Reading a refusal](@/guide/refusals.md).
+
+Lengths are in mm (inches in an inch document), feeds in mm/min (in/min).
+
+## Probe
+
+**For:** measuring the part on the machine with a spindle touch probe and
+either setting a work offset from what it finds or checking the part
+against the model. It cuts nothing and removes no stock.
+
+**The tool.** A touch probe; anything else is refused: "a probe operation
+mounts a touch probe, not a ...". The stylus ball's diameter is the
+tool's diameter.
+
+**Picks.** One feature on the Geometry tab seeds the operation; the pick
+writes the mode, directions and expected contact, and one undo takes it
+back:
+
+- a flat face: a **Face** touch against its outward normal;
+- a straight edge: an **Edge** touch on the side face under it;
+- a corner: an **Outside corner**, one X touch and one Y touch;
+- a round vertical wall or rim: a **Bore centre** or **Boss centre**.
+
+What the probe cannot touch honestly is refused: "the picked face is not
+planar - a face touch needs a flat face"; "the picked face looks down -
+the stylus only descends in Z; probe it from a side"; "the picked face
+stands ... off X, Y and Z - a probe touches along an axis"; "the picked
+wall is not vertical (a cone, fillet or tilted wall) - a bore or boss
+centre is found on a vertical round wall".
+
+| Tab | Setting | Default |
+|---|---|---|
+| Geometry | Find | Face (Edge, Outside corner, Bore centre, Boss centre) |
+| Geometry | Touch toward | -Z (a corner: X and Y touch directions, +Y for Y) |
+| Geometry | Radius (bore / boss) | 10 |
+| Geometry | Expected contact X / Y / Z | 0, 0, 0 (the pick sets it) |
+| Heights | Clearance (safe plane) | 25 above the stock top |
+| Passes | Approach clearance | 5 |
+| Passes | Probe distance | 1 |
+| Passes | Back-off | 1 |
+| Passes | Depth below edge / Corner inset | 3 / 5 |
+| Feeds | Seek feed / Measure feed | 300 / 30 |
+| Machine | Result | Set G54 (Report and stop, Set G54 to G59) |
+| Machine | Tolerance | 0.5 |
+
+Each touch is a fast seek, a back-off and a slow measuring re-probe; a
+centre is the mean of opposite wall touches. The **Probe distance** is a
+search limit past the expected contact, not a destination: the probe
+stops where it touches, and alarms if nothing trips by then.
+
+**What it writes.** The post writes each touch as a probing (skip) move,
+the back-off as an incremental move from wherever the stylus tripped, and
+the moves between touches as protected moves that stop on an unexpected
+contact. Then the result: with **Set G54..G59** the found position is
+written into that work offset; with **Report and stop** nothing is set.
+Either way, a found position further than **Tolerance** from the model
+stops the program with a message, and a touch that finds nothing alarms.
+The Fanuc, Haas, Heidenhain, Sinumerik, Mazak, Doosan, Tormach and Carvera
+posts write probing; a post script that cannot is refused by name
+("probing: this post script does not define onProbeMove - it cannot write
+a probing (skip) move, so the probe operation is refused").
+
+**The guards.**
+
+- Every stylus move is judged against the model: a ball that comes nearer
+  than its radius to the part anywhere before or after the expected
+  contact is a stylus driven through material, flagged as a gouge, and the
+  post is held. A modelled probe body is judged above the stylus too.
+- A probe distance over 2 mm is flagged ("probe distance ... mm at move
+  ...: the search may run that far past the expected contact, beyond the
+  2.000 mm a stylus is trusted to overtravel (the post is not held)").
+
+**Common refusals:** "the back-off must not exceed the approach
+clearance"; "probe feeds must be positive and the measuring feed no
+faster than the seek"; "an edge is probed along X or Y, not Z"; "a corner
+takes one X touch and one Y touch"; "a bore of radius ... mm has no room
+for a ... mm stylus ball and its back-off"; "the safe plane Z ... does not
+clear the probed feature (top ...) by the stylus ball and the approach";
+"the probe tolerance must be positive"; "the work offset to set must be
+one of G54..G59".

+
+The multi-axis kinds, Probe and Plasma Profile each have their own
+reference, with settings, defaults and common refusals:
+[Multi-axis operations](@/guide/operations-multiaxis.md),
+[Probing](@/guide/operations-probing.md) and
